_note: Content fragments (SGODOT-275, cross-city plan §6 on the 275 card). From P1 on, new data goes in a file of its own here, never into p0_content.json: <line>_<topic>.json in lower case (farm_*, fish_*, mine_*, cook_*, homestead_*, residents_*, requests_*, world_*, travel_*), shaped like the main table with the same top-level keys. The server (loadP0Content) and the client (P0Logic.content) merge the files in name order: objects key by key, arrays of objects with an id append by id; a key, an id or a scalar already there is an error, so a fragment adds and never changes an entry. Changing an existing entry is done in p0_content.json by the line that owns that block. Keys starting with _ are skipped. This file holds the travel line's data (亚瑟 / 蒙恬).

travel._landmarks: Landmark stamps (plan v2 §11.9.3 表 11-18, SGODOT-275): cluster id → its landmark and stamp art (assets/p0/stamps/<stamp>.png, 安其拉 from Figma 299:2955, 256 px; the nine open home cities outside the US drawn for the home pick, SGODOT-303). Mapped by the landmark's nearest member city (亚瑟: Space Center Houston stays with League City, 4.9 km, not Houston 34.8 km). Other first visits get a climate stamp.
travel._closed_countries: Countries whose cities do not open (q(189), SGODOT-305): the city table skips their clusters on the server (content.ts) and the client (P0Clusters), so they are on no map, search, Nearby list or fallback list and cannot be travelled to or picked as home. Their generated places stay as they are, so world.revision does not change.
